mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in the past month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST decline does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the past month signals strengthening economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 1% does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 8% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decline for two consecutive months, it signals a severe labor market downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 8% and PAYEMS declines for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of UNRATE > 8% and PAYEMS decline does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real final sales (RSAFS) for two consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS increase does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 0.5% and CPI (CPIAUCSL) is above 2.5% annualized, it signals a potential monetary policy misalignment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of low FEDFUNDS and high CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent market downturns.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high level of real GDP (GDPC1) relative to its 12-month moving average signals robust economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or GDPC1 relative strength does not correlate with subsequent market performance.
